identityTest.stableIdentity: A governed user journey remains identifiable across service substitutions, step revisions, channel changes, observation-point changes and SLO policy versions.
identityTest.versionIdentity: Changes to intended outcome, actor scope, ordered journey stages, entry or completion criteria, critical path or exclusions create immutable journey revisions while preserving historical evaluations.
identityTest.mastership: service owner, product owner or customer-experience authority

owns: stable user-journey identity and immutable revisions
intended user-visible outcome and actor or segment scope
ordered logical stages and completion criteria
service, application and channel participation bindings

references.purpose: Journey-level SLI and SLO commitments and evaluations
Service definitions participating in the journey
Qualified observation evidence for journey outcomes
Business applications or systems participating in the journey

excludes: process execution and individual user-session occurrence

invariants: User Journey identity is independent of any one service, application, channel, deployment or SLO policy.
Every journey revision states an intended user-visible outcome, actor scope, ordered stages and completion criteria.
Replacing a participating service changes a binding or successor revision and never silently changes journey identity.
Material changes to stages, outcome, entry criteria, completion criteria or exclusions create a successor revision.
Journey definitions never create user-session, process-execution or transaction occurrences.
Journey-level SLO evaluations pin the exact journey revision and observation points used.
Missing telemetry produces incomplete or unknown evaluation and never a successful journey outcome.
Participating services and applications retain their source identities and lifecycles.
A diagnostic component indicator never becomes a journey commitment without an explicit aggregation rule.
Journey success never proves contractual SLA compliance or business outcome without the relevant external authority.
Actor scope and privacy controls are explicit and never inferred from observed identifiers.
Retired journey identifiers and superseded revisions remain resolvable and are never recycled.
holds: Registry namespace and identifier allocation are pending and no identifier may be guessed.
